function: Channel modeling: reconstruct a wireless radiation field with 3D Gaussian splatting to synthesize receiver spatial spectra per TX position; RSSI and uplink-to-downlink CSI prediction case studies (pp. 1, 11-12).
system: Lab spatial spectrum: fixed RX with 4x4 array at 915 MHz, RFID TX moved; CSI case: 104-antenna BS (Argos), 52 subcarriers; RSSI case: single antenna; no RIS (pp. 10-12).
method: Two MLPs plus 3D Gaussian splatting (WRF-GS); WRF-GS+ adds a deformation MLP; supervised per-scene training with L1 plus SSIM loss (pp. 6-10).
data_channel: Measured: NeRF2 lab dataset (spatial spectra, TX positions, 915 MHz), public BLE RSSI dataset, and public Argos measured CSI dataset (104-antenna BS) (pp. 10-12).
test_conditions: NeRF2 lab: fixed test set, training size swept 200-4,800; BLE: 1,600 train and 400 test per RX; Argos: uplink subcarriers 1-26 to downlink 27-52, split not stated (pp. 10-12).
baselines: Non-learned: ray tracing, R2F2 (optimization). Learned: VAE, DCGAN, NeRF2, FIRE, OptML. RSSI also vs MRI (log-distance path-loss interpolation) (pp. 10-12).
metrics: SSIM of synthesized spatial spectra (CDF, median); rendering time per sample; RSSI prediction error (dB); CEA, channel estimation accuracy (dB), for downlink CSI (pp. 10-13).
complexity: Measured rendering time per spectrum: 0.008 s WRF-GS+, 0.005 s WRF-GS, versus 0.2 s NeRF2, 0.05 s VAE, 0.09 s DCGAN, 7 s ray tracing (p. 11, Fig. 12).
openness: Code: https://github.com/wenchaozheng/WRF-GSplus (p. 1); data: public NeRF2 lab, BLE and Argos datasets (pp. 10-12).
q1_support: p. 10: "We use an open-source dataset provided in NeRF2 [7]" obtained in a laboratory; p. 12: "public Argos channel dataset [33]" which "is collected in a real environment". Measured data.
q2_support: p. 10: "We maintain a consistent test dataset and randomly subsample the original training dataset"; p. 11: "measurements are used for training and the remaining 400 are used for testing" and "we train the proposed methods on the dataset of each RX". Held-out splits, size sweeps and per-RX retraining only.
q3_support: p. 12: R2F2 works "by solving an optimization problem to estimate the downlink CSI" (non-learned) and "FIRE is a deep learning method based on the VAE architecture" (learned); p. 12: "WRF-GS+ achieves a median CEA of 23.91 dB". Ray tracing, VAE, DCGAN, NeRF2 compared in SSIM (p. 10).
q4_support: p. 11: "WRF-GS+ achieves a processing time of 0.008s per sample", with the other methods' times listed (Fig. 12). Measured runtime.
q5_support: p. 1: "The code is available at https://github.com/wenchaozheng/WRF-GSplus"; also public datasets (p. 10: "open-source dataset provided in NeRF2"; p. 12: "public Argos channel dataset").
notes: Included under area 2: the learned function is neural channel modeling (spatial spectrum synthesis) plus downlink CSI prediction from uplink CSI in a 104-antenna system; reviewer to confirm that this counts as channel synthesis or prediction and not as an excluded function, since the RSSI case study is single-antenna and linked to positioning. q1 and q5 rest on measured public datasets and the released code. PDF is arXiv v4 (24 Mar 2025); its title matches the Crossref title of the DOI.
